title: arxiv_2511.09455v1
universal_lens: Synchronized multi-view video capture enables cross-modal spatial correspondence for robust player identification in dense American football scenes. The sovereign primitive unifies high-dimensional spatiotemporal tracking under severe occlusion and non-rigid motion blur. It models the American football field as a dynamic Riemannian manifold, where player trajectories are geodesics perturbed by stochastic collision operators. The handheld camera introduces a time-dependent diffeomorphism, requiring an invariant metric tensor to preserve topological continuity across frames.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updates on player states using multi-view likelihoods for real-time performance inference in high-density motion environments. GSI maps the bounding box annotations to a conformal prediction framework over the latent state space of player positions. By treating the 26 maximum bounding boxes per frame as a finite measure, we construct a Bayesian posterior over tracklet continuities. This allows for rigorous uncertainty quantification when distinguishing between highly correlated agents during rapid directional changes.
gse_mapping: Situation-aware state transitions driven by spatiotemporal player embeddings and re-ID confidence thresholds for tactical decision-making. GSE translates the play categories (pass, run, punt) into discrete state-transition matrices within a Hidden Markov Model. The phase progression from huddle to near-end defines the temporal boundaries of the transition kernel. Situational reasoning is achieved by evaluating the probability density of specific tactical primitives given the observed multi-object tracking outputs.

The core challenge identified in the text—tracking under rapid directional changes and frequent occlusions—is modeled as a stochastic differential equation governing the position X_t of each agent. The drift term \mu(X_t) encapsulates the strategic intent (e.g., running back path), while the diffusion term \sigma dW_t accounts for the unpredictable perturbations from physical collisions. The introduction of handheld camera motion adds a global, time-dependent transformation T_t: \Omega \to \Omega', which distorts the underlying metric. To recover true trajectories, we must estimate the inverse diffeomorphism T_t^{-1}, effectively stabilizing the video stream before applying standard multi-object tracking algorithms. The annotation process, yielding 188,711 bounding boxes across 11,411 frames, provides the empirical ground truth for training a neural network to approximate this stabilization and subsequent tracking. The maximum of 26 bounding boxes per frame establishes a hard constraint on the combinatorial complexity of the assignment problem, allowing for efficient Hungarian algorithm implementations despite the high occlusion rates. Ultimately, the dataset serves as a rich testbed for evaluating the robustness of tracking algorithms in extreme, dynamic environments, bridging the gap between controlled laboratory settings and chaotic real-world sports scenarios.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires inferring their internal state machines. A quarterback's trajectory is not random; it is a deliberate evasion path conditioned on the defensive line's pressure. Similarly, a receiver's route is a pre-planned geometric shape modified by defender proximity. Our theory of mind module posits that each player maintains a belief distribution over the ball's location and teammates' positions. By analyzing the historical bounding box data, we can reverse-engineer these beliefs, predicting future actions based on current spatial configurations. This goes beyond simple kinematic extrapolation, incorporating strategic intent derived from play types (pass, run, punt) and phases (huddle to near-end).
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity is enforced by ensuring that the visual features extracted for tracking are independent of the semantic play classification. If a model relies solely on jersey color to distinguish teams, it will fail under uniform lighting changes or against opponents with similar colors. We veto any feature set that exhibits high correlation with camera motion artifacts, preventing the tracker from latching onto background shifts rather than actual player movement. Furthermore, leakage from future frames into past predictions is strictly prohibited; the system must operate causally, mimicking a real-time broadcast analytics engine. This ensures that the derived primitives are robust and generalizable, not merely overfitting to the specific temporal quirks of the annotated dataset.
